title: Generically reduced embedded histories and local invariant calculus
statement: Over $\mathbf Q$, an embedded input is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] $X\hookrightarrow P$, with $P$ smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] and finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $X$ finite type and reduced at each generic point of an irreducible component [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. No global reducedness is imposed. A finite history records the ambient ordinary blowups [def-nagata-global-blowup], the actual scheme-theoretic strict transforms [def-nagata-strict-transform], the ideal centers, and their chronological order. Extensions preserve the entire earlier diagram and ideals; smooth comparisons are cartesian diagrams deleting exactly the empty pulled-back centers, including comparisons on intrinsic schemes using local ambient embeddings. Let $V$ be one linear order with least element $\bot$. A simultaneous assignment $\nu_H:X_H\to V$ generates its admissible histories from empty histories by reduced full positive maximum-center steps, open restriction and smooth pullback. A calculus consists of such an assignment, finite image and closed upper strata on each admissible history, regular [def-weil-regular-scheme] bottom locus, and extension at every nonbottom maximum. Each full reduced maximum center is nonempty, regular, nowhere dense, has coherent [pqf-def-coherent] ambient and intrinsic ideals, and avoids the inverse image of the original regular locus. The next ambient remains smooth, separated and finite type and its actual strict transform remains finite type and generically reduced. All-bottom histories have regular strict transform and regular inputs have no active stratum. Values and reduced ideals of every individual locally closed stratum agree under open and arbitrary smooth pullback, in both intrinsic schemes and ambient charts, with unit ideals for empty inverse images. Different embeddings of the same intrinsic history with the same ordered earlier ideals give equal values and reduced stratum ideals; these equalities respect further comparisons. Finally there is no infinite full-maximum history starting at an empty history. All inputs, including finite disjoint unions and the empty scheme, use the same value order. No cleanup steps after regularity are required.
